literal: At the time when evening spreads, bewildering the mind, the town, having become bewildered, suffers distress.
translation: At the hour when evening spreads, bewildering my mind, the entire town itself seems bewildered and suffers in deep distress.
modern: என் அறிவு மயங்கும்படியாக மாலைப் பொழுது வந்து பரவும்போது, இந்த ஊரே மயங்கித் துன்பத்தில் உழல்கிறது.
explanation: In this couplet, the lady describes the agonizing arrival of evening during separation. When evening (mālai) spreads (paṭartarum) at that specific time (pōḻtu), it bewilders (maruṇṭu) her mind (mati). In her intense grief, she projects her own sorrow onto her surroundings, perceiving that the entire town (pati) has also become bewildered (maruṇṭu) and is suffering (uḻakkum) in deep distress (paital). The repetition of the word 'maruṇṭu' (bewildered) emphasizes the overwhelming confusion and pain that the twilight hour brings to those separated from their loved ones.
